ns0:entry.ns0:title: docs(praxis): refresh stale statements; no internal path in the base …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
docs(praxis): refresh stale statements; no internal path in the base fixture (#5325)

* docs(praxis): the public checkpoint names, the LeRobot 0.7 lock, praxis-sim on PyPI

- The checkpoints are named by their public Hub repositories throughout the guide, the model card
  README, the examples README, code comments and test docstrings: `runwayml/praxis-1-droid-lerobot`
  is the released single-arm DROID checkpoint (54 GB, sharded), `runwayml/praxis-1-yam-lerobot` the
  bimanual checkpoint for two YAM arms, `runwayml/praxis-1-base-lerobot` the backbone and
  action-expert trunk without the heads of a rig. The earlier, unreleased DROID checkpoint of the
  results section is called that. Labels of training runs and export directories are gone.
- The page said LeRobot 0.7.0 locks transformers 5.22.1; main is LeRobot 0.7.1 and locks 5.22.2,
  which gives the same commands as 5.22.1 (checked on the DROID and the YAM checkpoint against the
  praxis repository), so the installation paragraph, the warning, the results and the parity notes
  name the 0.7 lock and both patch versions.
- `praxis-sim` is on PyPI (0.1.0, the code of the praxis repository's `packages/praxis-sim`): the
  vendoring note says so and the resources table gets a Simulator row. LeRobot has no environment
  for it yet.
- References to a private repository's pull requests and commits are replaced by the public
  praxis-1-oss `main` and the vendored commit the file headers name.
- `examples/praxis/README.md` lists `compute_norm_stats.py` and `init_heads.py` (the base
  checkpoint) and notes the converter's own `SHA256SUMS` and the base checkpoint's missing
  processors.

No code change: comments and docstrings only in the Python files.

* test(praxis): the base fixture's provenance names the public checkpoint

The base checkpoint fixture carried the provenance block of its training run, with a storage path
and a codename. The block now names the public Hub repository of the weights,
`runwayml/praxis-1-base-lerobot`, as the public config does, and describes the checkpoint in plain
words. Nothing reads the values: the config check only allows the key, and the base-checkpoint test
skips the block.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(policies): add Praxis-1 (#5321)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(policies): add Praxis-1 (#5321)

Add `praxis`, the LeRobot adapter of Praxis-1, Runway's open-weight World Action Model: a
chunk-causal video diffusion backbone (a 27B-parameter mixture-of-experts transformer) with an
action expert that denoises 24 Cartesian commands at 15 Hz alongside the next 1.6 s of video.

- The policy, its configuration and its processor steps in `lerobot/policies/praxis`, with the
  model code vendored under `praxis_core` (FlashAttention-4 and Triton attention backends).
- Inference with the single-arm DROID checkpoint and the bimanual YAM checkpoint.
- Fine-tuning through `lerobot-train` with the praxis objective, in full (FSDP) or with LoRA
  adapters through PEFT, and the `praxis_adamw` optimizer (AdamW with stochastic rounding for
  the bfloat16 weights).
- The base checkpoint: conversion, the heads of a rig and its normalization statistics.
- Datacenter and RTX Blackwell GPUs.
- Batched Euler, quaternion and matrix conversions on `Rotation`.
- The `praxis` extra, examples, the guide, a model card section and tests.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(processor): refuse rename_map collisions instead of silently drop…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(processor): refuse rename_map collisions instead of silently dropping a key (#5316)

Two keys renamed to the same name (e.g. action.cartesian -> action on a dataset
that already has action) were resolved differently per code path: make_policy
read the action names from the first match, while the features, stats, batches
and observations kept the last one. Every rename path now goes through
rename_keys, which raises and suggests renaming the existing key as well.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(policies): sharded safetensors checkpoints in the transformers l…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(policies): sharded safetensors checkpoints in the transformers layout (#5306)

* feat(policies): support sharded safetensors checkpoints

Add opt-in sharded saving and local or Hub loading while keeping the
single-file default. Give custom policy loaders access to all shards
without writing a merged temporary checkpoint.

Check missing and unexpected keys after loading hooks, handle tied and
empty tensors correctly, and include sharded checkpoints in Trackio
uploads. Document the scope of support and cover the loading paths with
regression tests.

* fix(policies): read shards per key and surface Hub errors

Filtered checkpoint loads were materializing every tensor in a shard, and a
non-404 Hub failure was rewritten as a missing checkpoint.

* fix(policies): load shards when the checkpoint hook is implemented

Keeping a legacy single-file hook was enough to reject a sharded checkpoint.
Also record that DCP conversion stays one file, and attach config.json to a
single-file Trackio artifact.
